newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed, new crop down on acreage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed, new crop down on acreage.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed on Wednesday with nearbys up on ideas of improving export and domestic demand but new crop was down on expectations U.S. corn plantings will increase, traders said.

Traders pointed to ideas U.S. hog production would grow to make up for a drop in Taiwan's herd due to foot and mouth disease. Taiwan on Wednesday ordered the slaughter of all hogs, even healthy ones, at farms affected by the outbreak.
"There is some fear that this hog (expansion) number could be a little bit bigger than people think," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities.
Expansion in the U.S. pork industry would mean increased feed demand, traders said.

New crop months were pressured by ideas 1997 corn plantings would be larger than last year. Analysts expected Monday's USDA prospective plantings report to show corn acreage at roughly 80.92 million acres, above last year's acreage of 79.49 million.
Quarterly stocks as of March 1 were also expected to grow to 4.565 billion bushels from 3.8 billion last year.
Corn closed three cents per bushel higher to 1/4 cent lower with May up three at $3.05-1/4.
Traders said activity was subdued and desribed the mood as "nervous" ahead of Monday's USDA quarterly stocks and prospective plantings report.
Volume in the corn pit was estimated at 46,000 contracts, below Tuesday's volume of 51,451 contracts.
"We were seeing more evening up kind of trade," Roose said. "People were not really willing to put on big new positions."

Export news was supportive as South Korea bought 105,000 tonnes of U.S. corn on Monday. Trade sources expected Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report to show 400,000 to 700,000 tonnes of corn sold.
Chartists said moving average signals were negative for May corn put positive for the July.Resistance was pegged at $3.06-1/2 in the May with support at $3.02-3/4.

On the day, Cargill Inc bought at least two million bushels July and one million May. Term Commodities bought one million each May and July. Farmers Commodities Corp and Continental Grain were also said to be buyers.
Griffin Trading sold five million bushels December.
In options, Continental Grain bought 600 December $3.00 calls and 600 December $3.00 puts at 47-3/4 to 48 cents. Continental also sold 500 December $3.60 calls at 7-3/4 cents.
Traders also said Continental bought another 600 July $3.00 calls and sold 600 July $2.70 puts at 15-1/4 to 15-3/4 cents.
